title: 1 Samuel 26
paragraphs: ¹ The Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Is not David hiding on the hill of Hakilah, which faces Jeshimon?" ² So Saul went down to the Desert of Ziph, with his three thousand select Israelite troops, to search there for David.

⁶ David spoke to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, saying, "Who will go down with me to Saul's camp?" Abishai said, "I'll go with you." ⁷ So David and Abishai crept into the camp at night. Saul lay sleeping inside the camp, his spear driven into the ground near his head, with Abner and the troops sleeping around him. ⁸ Abishai whispered to David, "God has handed your enemy over to you today. Let me pin him to the ground with his own spear — one thrust will do it." ⁹ But David said, "Don't kill him. Who could raise a hand against the LORD's anointed and go unpunished? ¹⁰ As surely as the LORD lives, the LORD himself will strike him down, or his time will come and he'll die naturally, or he'll fall in battle. But not by my hand."

¹¹ "God forbid that I should lift my hand against the LORD's anointed. Just take the spear by his head and the water jug, and let's go." ¹² So David took the spear and the water jug from beside Saul's head, and they slipped away. No one saw them, no one knew, no one woke up — they were all fast asleep, because the LORD had put them into a deep sleep. ¹³ David crossed to the far side and stood on top of a hill at a distance, with a wide stretch of ground between them. ¹⁴ He called out to the troops and to Abner son of Ner, "Abner! Aren't you going to answer?" Abner called back, "Who are you to shout at the king?" ¹⁵ David said, "You're supposed to be a great man — there's no one like you in Israel, right? So why haven't you protected your lord the king? Someone came in to kill the king your lord tonight."

¹⁶ "What you've done is not right. As the LORD lives, you deserve to die for not protecting the LORD's anointed, your master. Look — where is the king's spear? Where is the water jug that was beside his head?" ¹⁷ Saul recognized David's voice and said, "Is that your voice, my son David?" David answered, "It is, my lord the king. ¹⁸ Why does my lord keep pursuing his servant? What have I done? What wrong have I committed? ¹⁹ Please, my lord the king, hear me out. If the LORD has stirred you up against me, then let an offering satisfy him. But if it's men who have turned you against me, then may they be cursed before the LORD — for they have driven me out today so that I can have no share in the LORD's inheritance, telling me to go serve other gods. ²⁰ Don't let my blood fall to the ground far from the LORD's presence. The king of Israel has come out to hunt a single flea — like someone hunting a partridge in the mountains."

²¹ Then Saul said, "I have sinned. Come back, my son David. I won't harm you again, because you valued my life today. I have acted like a fool and made a terrible mistake." ²² David replied, "Here is the king's spear — send one of your men over to get it. ²³ The LORD rewards each person for their faithfulness and integrity. He delivered you into my hands today, but I refused to raise my hand against the LORD's anointed. ²⁴ Just as I valued your life today, may the LORD value mine and rescue me from all my troubles." ²⁵ Saul said to David, "Bless you, my son David. You will do great things and surely succeed." Then David went on his way, and Saul returned home.
